      What is (Islam ❤️)  ?
      
      Islam is the name of the religion, or more properly the ‘way of life’, which God (Allah) has revealed and which was practiced by all of the Prophets and Messengers of God that He sent to mankind.  Even the name stands out unique among other
      
      distorted religions in that it means a state of being; it does not refer to any particular person, such as Christianity, Buddhism or Zoroastrianism; a tribe like Judaism; or a nation like Hinduism.  The root Arabic word from which Islam is derived implies peace, safety, salutation, protection, blamelessness, wholesomeness, submission, acceptance, surrender, and salvation.  Islam specifically means being in the state of submission to God, worshipping Him Alone, and reverently accepting and obeying His Law.  Through this submission, the peace, security, and wholesome well-being implied in its literal meaning is achieved.  Hence, a Muslim or Muslimah is a person (male or female) in that state of submission.  A person’s Islam weakens through sins, ignorance, and wrong-doing, and becomes nullified in totality by associating partners with God or disbelieving in Him.

      What is (Islam ❤️)  ?
      
      Islam is the name of the religion, or more properly the ‘way of life’, which God (Allah) has revealed and which was practiced by all of the Prophets and Messengers of God that He sent to mankind.  Even the name stands out unique among other
      
      distorted religions in that it means a state of being; it does not refer to any particular person, such as Christianity, Buddhism or Zoroastrianism; a tribe like Judaism; or a nation like Hinduism.  The root Arabic word from which Islam is derived implies peace, safety, salutation, protection, blamelessness, wholesomeness, submission, acceptance, surrender, and salvation.  Islam specifically means being in the state of submission to God, worshipping Him Alone, and reverently accepting and obeying His Law.  Through this submission, the peace, security, and wholesome well-being implied in its literal meaning is achieved.  Hence, a Muslim or Muslimah is a person (male or female) in that state of submission.  A person’s Islam weakens through sins, ignorance, and wrong-doing, and becomes nullified in totality by associating partners with God or disbelieving in Him.

      What is (Islam ❤️)  ?
      
      Islam is the name of the religion, or more properly the ‘way of life’, which God (Allah) has revealed and which was practiced by all of the Prophets and Messengers of God that He sent to mankind.  Even the name stands out unique among other
      
      distorted religions in that it means a state of being; it does not refer to any particular person, such as Christianity, Buddhism or Zoroastrianism; a tribe like Judaism; or a nation like Hinduism.  The root Arabic word from which Islam is derived implies peace, safety, salutation, protection, blamelessness, wholesomeness, submission, acceptance, surrender, and salvation.  Islam specifically means being in the state of submission to God, worshipping Him Alone, and reverently accepting and obeying His Law.  Through this submission, the peace, security, and wholesome well-being implied in its literal meaning is achieved.  Hence, a Muslim or Muslimah is a person (male or female) in that state of submission.  A person’s Islam weakens through sins, ignorance, and wrong-doing, and becomes nullified in totality by associating partners with God or disbelieving in Him.

      What is (Islam ❤️)  ?
      
      Islam is the name of the religion, or more properly the ‘way of life’, which God (Allah) has revealed and which was practiced by all of the Prophets and Messengers of God that He sent to mankind.  Even the name stands out unique among other
      
      distorted religions in that it means a state of being; it does not refer to any particular person, such as Christianity, Buddhism or Zoroastrianism; a tribe like Judaism; or a nation like Hinduism.  The root Arabic word from which Islam is derived implies peace, safety, salutation, protection, blamelessness, wholesomeness, submission, acceptance, surrender, and salvation.  Islam specifically means being in the state of submission to God, worshipping Him Alone, and reverently accepting and obeying His Law.  Through this submission, the peace, security, and wholesome well-being implied in its literal meaning is achieved.  Hence, a Muslim or Muslimah is a person (male or female) in that state of submission.  A person’s Islam weakens through sins, ignorance, and wrong-doing, and becomes nullified in totality by associating partners with God or disbelieving in Him.

      What is (Islam ❤️)  ?
      
      Islam is the name of the religion, or more properly the ‘way of life’, which God (Allah) has revealed and which was practiced by all of the Prophets and Messengers of God that He sent to mankind.  Even the name stands out unique among other
      
      distorted religions in that it means a state of being; it does not refer to any particular person, such as Christianity, Buddhism or Zoroastrianism; a tribe like Judaism; or a nation like Hinduism.  The root Arabic word from which Islam is derived implies peace, safety, salutation, protection, blamelessness, wholesomeness, submission, acceptance, surrender, and salvation.  Islam specifically means being in the state of submission to God, worshipping Him Alone, and reverently accepting and obeying His Law.  Through this submission, the peace, security, and wholesome well-being implied in its literal meaning is achieved.  Hence, a Muslim or Muslimah is a person (male or female) in that state of submission.  A person’s Islam weakens through sins, ignorance, and wrong-doing, and becomes nullified in totality by associating partners with God or disbelieving in Him.

      What is (Islam ❤️)  ?
      
      Islam is the name of the religion, or more properly the ‘way of life’, which God (Allah) has revealed and which was practiced by all of the Prophets and Messengers of God that He sent to mankind.  Even the name stands out unique among other
      
      distorted religions in that it means a state of being; it does not refer to any particular person, such as Christianity, Buddhism or Zoroastrianism; a tribe like Judaism; or a nation like Hinduism.  The root Arabic word from which Islam is derived implies peace, safety, salutation, protection, blamelessness, wholesomeness, submission, acceptance, surrender, and salvation.  Islam specifically means being in the state of submission to God, worshipping Him Alone, and reverently accepting and obeying His Law.  Through this submission, the peace, security, and wholesome well-being implied in its literal meaning is achieved.  Hence, a Muslim or Muslimah is a person (male or female) in that state of submission.  A person’s Islam weakens through sins, ignorance, and wrong-doing, and becomes nullified in totality by associating partners with God or disbelieving in Him.

      ‎بسم الله والحمدلله والصلاة والسلام على رسول الله أمّا بعد فإنّي أدعوك بدعاية الإسلام، فأسلم لله يُسلّمك في الدنيا والآخرة وإن توليت فإنّي أخاف عليك عذاب الله يوم القيامة، فانظر الى نفسك كيف أنشأك من نطفة وثبّتك في جدار الرحم ووصلك بالحبل السرّي وأمدك بالغذاء والأكسجين وحفظك بالكيس الامنيوني ثم لما خرجت الى هذه الدنيا درّ في ضرع امك اللبن تماما بما تحتاج، ثم هو خلق لك الشمس وقدّر حرارتها ومسافتها الى الارض بما يناسبك وجعل ضوءها يناسب بؤبؤ عينك فيضيق ويتسع في نطاق درجة ضوء الشمس، وأدار الأرض دوراناً أنشأ الليل بما يناسب نومك تماماً، ثم هو قدّر خواصّ الماء بما يناسب معاشك ومعاش الخلق، فيتبخر الماء من حرارة الشمس، فيصير سحاباً، ثم يحرّك الريح تحمل السحاب اليك لتشرب الماء وينبت لك من الحب اليابس ألوان الطعام والفواكه والحبوب، فانظر وتأمل، فكل شيءٍ يَشهد بواحدانيته وحكمته وقدرته، وانظر الى أكبر مجرات هذا الكون الى أصغر ذراته كلّه يسير بنظام متقن يدل على إرادة واحدة ولو كان أكثر من إله لفسدت السموات والأرض، وعيسى عبدالله ورسوله وما اتخذ الله ولداً، والإله أزلي ليس له بداية، والولد له بداية، فلا يمكن أن يكون لله ولد، بل الله رب كل شيء وهو القاهر فوق عباده 
      ‎وقد أرسل إلينا رسلاً برحمته وأيدهم بمعجزات تقطع بصدقهم، وخاتم رسله محمدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم وأيّده بمعجزات كثيرة تواترت تواتراً يفيد القطع بنبوته، فنبع الماء من بين أصابعه وأبرأ الأعمى بدعاءه وكُثّر الطعام بين يديه وحنّ له الجذع، وبشّرت بنبوته التوراة والانجيل وأنزل الله على محمد القرآن وجعله معجزاً وبينةً وتبياناً لكل شيء،
      ‎فإنّي أخوّفك من الله وأخوّفك من جهنم 
      ‎وأدعوك بدعاية الإسلام، بأن تخضع لأوامر الله فإنه أمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى ونهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي، وأمرك بأن تشهد الشهادتين وتقيم الصلاة وتؤتي الزكاة وتصوم رمضان وتحج البيت، وأن استغفر الله ثم تب اليه يمتعك في هذه الدنيا متاعاً حسناً الى أجل مسمى وإن توليت فإني أخاف عليك عذاب يوم كبير، 
      ‎والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

  MSA  is easiest , MSA or Modern Standard Arabic ; If you want to learn Arabic I adivce you to start with Modern standard Arabicc ( MSA ) and you will understand any other dialect ;  MSA (also known as Fusha) is derived directly from the Quran, but it is also the language of contemporary news media, the academic world, and much of Arabic literature. ; Learn the  Fosha (MSA) Arabic first. Learning different Arabic dialects will only be useful based on the Arab country dialect that you learnt. Whereas, learning the standard Arabic (Fosha)  can be used in all arab countries and every Arab will understand what your saying. Also, everything is written in the standard Fosha Arabic in all Arab countries. It's only the talking and speaking which is different.

  Fun fact: Malay language previously use hijaiyyah lettering called Jawi. Additional letter is included to fit the language. Malay language used to be the lingua franca during the Malacca Sultanate (Malacca Straits area). Letters like nya (nun with three dots for ng sound) and va (wau with dot for v sound) are an example. Now it is changed to alphabets since it is the current trading language.

    ↳ **@someoneelse6934** (👍9 · 2024-08-12) — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xg1UqrQMDQ&lc=UgxEcu2invF1vrLIEjF4AaABAg.9p28Tw2DfOiA-9UvqkNifc
      Very solid tips. I love languages and have dived into 7 so far. Arabic is next on my list, which is why I stumbled across this. A couple other key tips that help me get started quickly: 1) learn the most common phrases and nouns that you can use everyday. Then as you learn them you can mix/match to build new phrases. The big thing is to learn phrases (or chunks) not simply one word. So for example some of the first chunks I will learn in any new language include the following. Note that I mix in different pronouns with the phrases for practice: I need a little coffee, you want a lot of things, she has a little money, I must sleep tomorrow, he could sleep today, they slept yesterday….  The sooner you can start talking these “baby phrases” the sooner you can start having at least small conversations…. Which lead to bigger conversations. Think like a small child. That is how they learn, not by studying hours with a book but by actually building small, awkward sentences (at first) and learning how to build them. “I want coffee” eventually grows into —> “I want more of that coffee” —> which grows into —> “That coffee e had yesterday was amazing! I want more of it, when I can get it”.  The absolute key is to only spend energy on chunk phrases that you will actually use in day to day like at first.

    ↳ **@hommedetowne4253** (👍3 · 2023-08-12) — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xg1UqrQMDQ&lc=Ugzt4s_QnIsM2bs6eRJ4AaABAg.9mFESih3f8m9mP_Us_PYIo
      I'm a non Arab whose intention for learning Arabic was to understand Quran, Hadith, and the classical islamic literary tradition (fiqh, kalam, adab, etc.)
      I first started studying Arabic about 25 years now. My advice for what you seek, don't scorn learning spoken Arabic dialects. It will help you learn fusha in many ways. For one, it will enable you to actually communicate with other Arabs, including teachers. Which will only help your journey of Ilm. Two, Arabiyya is like an ocean. Every root has a huge semantic field of meaning. You can ONLY get a good intuitive understanding of many words in the Quran and ahadith and akhbar and athar by developing a good feel for how words are used in spoken language. Many times a term in 3miyya or darija is an idiom that's sort of a frozen expression originally from fusha. There's thousands of little terms in spoken dialectical Arabic that show usages the shed light on the Quran and hadith. Ways of using a word that sheds light on subtle shades of Quranic usage. To find the meaning otherwise you'd have to pore through Taj al Arus or Ibn Manzur to connect the dots.
      
      Many of us non Arab Muslims have an idea that it's not useful learning spoken Arabic to understand the Quran, and that's  wrong.   I'm saying this as someone who has  studied Arabic for almost 25 years of my life. I began my journey very much as you, so you can either take or leave my advice as you see fit, but I've been where you're at. 
      
      The only real danger in learning spoke with our legs first, and knowing this danger you can correct it, is that it's possible to develop certain habits of pronunciation and understanding of grammar that don't fully carry-over. You can develop a few bad habits but if you know that in advance you can adjust for that.

      While I respect this perspective- I think that for people who are interested in making conversation, learning MSA from the beginning is not an ideal choice. Yes, it is somewhat similar to spoken dialects- but spoken dialects are also similar to one another. And in my opinion, any serious student of an Arabic dialect will be able to read Arabic script and voice the proper pronunciations of ق، غ، ظ etc, relatively easily after a few months of study. 
      It is true that there are more high-quality learning materials available for MSA than for spoken dialects- so for people who are more interested in reading or academic-style (as opposed to conversational) learning, MSA may be the better option. But for me, the goal of learning Arabic was always being able to speak with other people- and I would argue that studying a spoken dialect from the start is the best way to do that.

      I'm half Egyptian, but grew up barely speaking Arabic. I decided to learn it and also had to make a choice. I decided to start with the dialect and am so glad I did. This obviously, as Brian said, depends on your goals firstly, but I also found that over time, through the dialect, a lot of MSA words came up anyways and I am now learning MSA and I honestly think that it would've been so much harder had I done it the other way around.       @ If you learn Tunisian you can communicate with Moroccans and Algerians easily, I can also usually communicate with other Arabs from the Levantine etc easily with my Tunisian.  It’s funny because for example if you learn formal Arabic AND French, you’d be able to speak with every single African and middle eastern country even sub Saharan African since they speak French in schools, so that’s really useful in general, and any formal (fusha) Arabic word that isn’t used in Tunisia or Morocco or Algeria you’d still be able to communicate with them because THEY would know the formal Arabic word, they would for sure tell you the North African version because they’re very proud of their language, the other cool thing is if you didn’t have the word in Arabic, you could use a French word and that would be easy to help bridge any language barrier since French is their second language in those 3 countries.
      
      When I was learning to speak Tunisian if I didn’t know something my MIL was saying in Tunisian I would ask her to tell me the word in French, that helped a lot.  
      
      I do wish I knew formal Arabic because it would be more versatile and allow me to more easily communicate with most Arabs from any country.  My Tunisian is fluent and it’s hard for me at the market when I say “alouch” for lamb, thinking all Arabs use that word, and then find out most other Arab countries call it “harrouf”, because I’m at the market asking the guy “what’s harrouf??” And he’s like “lamb 👀 “ lol
      
      My husband knows “harrouf” is lamb in formal Arabic (since they learn formal Arabic in school), so he would know how to change his words at the store or a restaurant, but now I find myself using Tunisian words and not knowing there’s a different word and I wish I had more proper Arabic knowledge.
      
      I do LOVE being able to speak North African, they are a wild bunch with such a fun language, since the dialect is so specific it feels really fun when I can speak fluently with North Africans.
      
      So, long answer long (sorry lol), super useful to know formal Arabic and French, and will make it easy to learn Tunisian or any other North African dialect, French is also helpful, learning Tunisian SPECIFICALLY is really useful to master the North African language, since I know Tunisian I can fluently speak with North Africans (Moroccan or Algerian), but not all Arabs.  
      
      If you learn Tunisian you’d still be able to use the language to build your Arabic skills.
      
      Both strategies have benefits! 
      
      I also feel like Tunisians use the LEAST amount of formal Arabic just from my experience talking to other North Africans, but that could technically not be true, I’m not sure.  I feel like Tunisian has a lot of slang, so if you learn Tunisian you can learn anything I swear. lol
      
      💕

      @BrianWilesOfficial  تزييف للحقيقة بقصد أو بدون قصد، الأمويين لم يغزوا شبه الجزيرة الإيبرية، بل استنجد شعبها  بالمسلمين من ظلم ملك القوط لأن شبه الجزيرة الأيبيرية كانت تخضع لحكم الغزاة بإستمرار.
      
      وبعد سقوط الدولة الأموية وقيام الدولة العباسية هرب أخر وريث لبني أمية إلى افريقيا ثم إلى شبه الجزيرة الإيبيرية حيث يحكم جزء منها ماتبقى من حكم الخلافة الأموية.
      
      ولم يتوسعوا إلا بعد إستنجاد شعبها بحاكم المسلمين هناك ورؤية عدله والدليل على ذلك أن المسلمين سيطروا على مجمل أراضي شبه الجزيرة الإيبيرية واهتموا بقوة الجيش والإسطول البحري.
      
      واضاقت الخناق على مملكة ليون ولم تدخلها وتوقف الزحف بأمر من حكام المسلمين لأن الإسلام ينص على تحريم قتال من يطلب السلام ولا يقاتلنا، وكانوا يدفعون الجزية للمسلمين لأسباب سياسية.
      
      كانوا يفرضون الجزية لضمان حمايتهم وعدم التدخل في شؤونهم ولسلامة اراضي الأندلس إذا نقضوا العهد، وهذا يحد من قوتهم فلا ينقلبوا عليهم،  وكان بمقدورهم إسقاط مملكة ليون.
      
      إن امعنت النظر بالتاريخ سترى ضعف مملكة ليون ومحاصرة المسلمين لها دون دخولها وهذا بسبب تعاليم ديننا للتعايش مع الدول الجوار إن أرادت السلام، والدليل الأخر على عدل المسلمين هو وجود كنائس المسيحيين ومعابد اليهود بالأندلس وتعايشهم مع العرب والمسلمين.
      
       والحقيقة أن مسمى "حروب الإستعادة" ماهي إلا كذبه ليبرروا بطشهم بسكان الأندلس وقتلهم وتعذيبهم وتهجيرهم وجرائمهم بإجبارهم بإعتناق دينهم، فهم لم يكونوا السكان الأصليين لشبه الجزيرة الإيبرية بل كانوا مجرد غزاة قبل حكم المسلمين وبعده.
      
       الله وحد المسلمين وأعزهم عندما كانوا متمسكين بطاعة الله، وفرقهم واذلهم عندما نسوا الله وانغمسوا بالمعازف والشهوات، هذه حكمة الله ولكل بداية نهاية.

      @SmthAbout.Money.SmellsLikeLove  that's what the Turkish Language Association would like you to think. Not only do they count the words derived from an Arabic/foreign word as Turkish words (for example they'd count the word "cevap" as a loan word, but all the words derived from it like "cevapsız, cevaplamak,..." as Turkish words, which adds to the illusion of there only being a few loan words), but they also tried to replace a lot of loan words with Turkish alternatives to no avail because a lot of these loan words are still being widely used in everyday life. So regardless of what the TLA states, the daily use of Arabic loan words in Turkish is a lot more than just 5%, and if you can't see that than you're the one being delusional.

Had there only been 5% Arabic words, I wouldn't have been able to pick it up in a couple months now would I?

        وقولي ان فرنسا هي من بثت تلك السموم   ليس يعني انه خدع بها الامازيغ فقط بل حتى العرب    لكن بما ان الأمر متعلق بنواحكم على لغتكم التي لم  يكن لها   قاعدة لتصمد عليها.  لأنها تحتاج إلى معيرة وتقعيد في كل جوانبها الصرفية والمعجمية والتركيبية  فقد خصصة ذكركم  ، و عند وصول العرب الأقحاح   إلى بلاد المغرب كانت  الأمازيغية كما هي  لهجة  بدون قواعد  يعني مثل الدارجة  العربية التي نتحدثها  اليوم  بدون قواعد او أسس  وهذا واقع لا ننكره  لذلك إزاحة اللهجات التي ليس لها قواعد اسهل مما تتوقع و لا تحتاج  لبطش او قوة لتندثر  ستنصهر لوحدها مع الزمن  مع اي تداخل  بين القوميات  ولا شك انه في كل 10 سنوات تموت عشرات اللغات   واذا اردت التأكد اكتب فقط في محرك البحث  إندثار اللغات  او  موت اللغة. لتطالع  الدراسات   وبعضها يقول انه خلال 100 سنة ستختفي نصف اللغات  فلم تحتاج لإندثارها   قوة كما تكذبون     
      طبعا لتفهم اعطيك مثال عن اللغة الإنجليزية  فعل تظن ان هي نفسها التي كتب بها  شكسبير   رواياته لا يا هذا  فهي تحتاج لمتخصصين  لفهمها و لن يفهما عوام الناس اليوم   فقد تغيرة قواعدها و اندثر الكثير مصطلحاتها.  
      اما عن فتح الاندلس فمص ملح و كل تبن  لتشبع غرورك    فقد فتحها  مسلمين من العرب و العجم  من شتى الاعراق  تحت  إمارة الدولة الأموية. بقيادة  مجاهد امازيغي  الذي كان بدوره تحت امرة مجاهد عربي  فهم نالوا  مناهم . وانت ابقى  طرطر    ولا نحتاج لرد هنا على غلك المكبوت  فقد سد منافذ الفهم عندك  فانت اشبه بآلة مبرمجة  ترسل ولا تستقبل 
       ولن اعطيك  وقت من عندي  لا تستحقه من الاساس       
      مت بغيضك
